full_text_en:
Shijiazhuang Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Wang Haisheng — case of intentional injury

[Ruling Summary]

Although the defendant's conduct constitutes the crime of intentional injury, in view of his minor subjective culpability, ordinary means of injury, and minor criminal circumstances, a sentence below the statutory punishment may be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Article 63, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law.

Criminal Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Xing Fu Zi No. 239

Defendant Wang Haisheng, male, born August 2, 1952, Han ethnicity, native of Pingshan County, Hebei Province, primary school education, farmer, residing in Pangjiapu Village, Pingshan County. Arrested on April 12, 2002. Currently in custody.

The Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province tried the case where the Shijiazhuang Municipal People's Procuratorate charged the defendant Wang Haisheng with intentional injury, and the plaintiff in the incidental civil action filed an incidental civil action. On January 26, 2003, it rendered the criminal附带 civil judgment (2002) Shi Xing Chu Zi No. 166, finding the defendant Wang Haisheng guilty of intentional injury, sentencing him to ten years' imprisonment and deprivation of political rights for three years; and ordering him to compensate the plaintiff in the incidental civil action for economic losses in the amount of RMB 5,000. After the judgment was pronounced, Wang Haisheng refused to accept it and appealed. The Hebei High People's Court, on September 11, 2003, rendered the criminal ruling (2003) Ji Xing Yi Zhong Zi No. 498, setting aside the original judgment and remanding the case for retrial. The Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court, on November 7, 2003, rendered the criminal附带 civil judgment (2003) Shi Xing Chu Zi No. 262, finding the defendant Wang Haisheng guilty of intentional injury, sentencing him to ten years' imprisonment and deprivation of political rights for two years; and ordering him to compensate the plaintiff in the incidental civil action in the amount of RMB 5,000. After the judgment was pronounced, Wang Haisheng refused to accept it and appealed. The Hebei High People's Court, on June 24, 2004, rendered the criminal judgment (2004) Ji Xing Yi Zhong Zi No. 176, finding the defendant Wang Haisheng guilty of intentional injury, sentencing him to three years' imprisonment below the statutory punishment, and submitted the case to this Court for approval in accordance with the law. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and reviewed the case. The review is now concluded.

The following facts were confirmed upon review: On the afternoon of March 8, 2002, after a verbal altercation between the families of the defendant Wang Haisheng and the victim Xia Xiulan over a trivial matter, Wang Haisheng and his elder and younger brothers went to a ridge of earth on the west side of Xia Xiulan's house and exchanged curses with Xia Xiulan, who was in her own yard. When Xia Xiulan climbed a ladder in the yard to curse Wang Haisheng, Wang Haisheng threw clods of earth and bricks at Xia Xiulan while she was on the ladder, causing Xia Xiulan to fall from the ladder to the ground, resulting in subarachnoid hemorrhage, cerebral hemorrhage, and brainstem hemorrhage, leading to death.

The above facts are confirmed by the record of scene inspection, forensic scientific examination report, and witness testimony, and are confessed by the defendant Wang Haisheng. The evidence is sufficient for affirmation.

This Court holds that the defendant Wang Haisheng's act of throwing clods of earth or bricks at the victim while she was on a ladder, causing her to fall from the ladder and die, constitutes the crime of intentional injury. The facts found in the judgments of the first and second instances are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, and the conviction is accurate. The trial procedures were lawful. In view of the defendant Wang Haisheng's minor subjective culpability, ordinary means of injury, and minor criminal circumstances, the second instance's sentence of three years' imprisonment below the statutory punishment for intentional injury is appropriate. In accordance with Article 63, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law of the PRC and Article 270 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, it is ruled as follows:

Approve the criminal judgment of the Hebei High People's Court (2004) Ji Xing Yi Zhong Zi No. 176, which sentenced the defendant Wang Haisheng to three years' imprisonment for the crime of intentional injury.

This ruling shall become legally effective upon service.

Presiding Judge: Li Yanming

Acting Judge: Wu Wenhe

Acting Judge: Song Ying

January 10, 2005

Clerk: Liu Shiqian

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Li Yanming, Senior Judge: Born in 1956, holds a bachelor's degree, served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 1993.
